features.description: Measure and optimize Florabase resource efficiency for self-hosted deployment
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible production-like baseline documents idle and representative operator workflows: startup and an idle authenticated session; Dashboard; BotanicalIdentity, SeedLot, Sowing, Plant or PlantGroup, Supplier, Location, and Geography directories and details; Events, Photos, lineage, provenance map, explicitly loaded occurrence map, and representative create or edit work. The workload measures process or container CPU and memory, startup stabilization, frontend initial transfer and lazy chunks, API and important database query counts, representative response time, media and map loading, and production image and process footprint where practical without relying only on synthetic microbenchmarks

Measured backend and PostgreSQL hotspots are reviewed for N+1 or redundant queries, unnecessary serialization or payload, repeated expensive queries, connection and memory behavior, and representative query plans; indexes or tuning are added only when workload evidence and appropriate EXPLAIN or ANALYZE support them, without speculative denormalization, materialized views, or generic tuning

Measured frontend, media, and map hotspots are reviewed for production bundle and chunk cost, the existing Vite chunk-size advisory, useful code splitting and lazy loading, unnecessary renders or duplicate API requests, oversized original images where bounded thumbnails fit, lazy local and external Photos behavior, hidden map instances, and map or provider traffic on unrelated navigation; the advisory threshold is not raised merely to hide a warning

Repeated navigation and extended idle use are checked for event-listener, map-instance, timer, request, retained-data, client-cache, session, and database-connection growth; CPU, memory, and requests stabilize without unnecessary polling or render loops, and only demonstrated leaks or resource hotspots are changed without altering domain semantics, security, or privacy or adding broad caching infrastructure

The production Compose stack is assessed for modest self-hosted hardware using measured CPU, memory, network, database, image-size, startup, package, process, and duplicate-work costs; footprint changes preserve reproducible builds, security updates, and needed operability, with no arbitrary hardware guarantee set before measurement

After focused optimization, the same representative workload is re-measured against the baseline; material improvements, remaining costs, practical small-installation resource expectations, and any meaningful regressions across measured dimensions are documented, with evidence-based regression budgets added only where justified
